title: Equivalent Polynomial Forms
student_objective: I can rewrite first- and second-degree polynomial expressions in equivalent forms using the distributive property.
teacher_objective: Diagnose distribution, sign, like-term, greatest-common-factor, multi-step simplification, equivalence, property, and geometric-model errors.

concept_cards.title: Equivalent means equal for every input
concept_cards.content: Equivalent expressions may look different, but they produce the same value for every allowed value of the variable.

concept_cards.title: Distribute to every term
concept_cards.content: Multiply the factor outside parentheses by every term inside, including each sign.

concept_cards.title: Combine only like terms
concept_cards.content: Terms combine only when their variable parts and exponents match exactly.

concept_cards.title: Reverse distribution
concept_cards.content: A common factor can be extracted: ab+ac=a(b+c). The expanded and common-factor forms are equivalent.

concept_cards.title: Verify equivalence
concept_cards.content: Use algebra to rewrite one form into the other. Substitution can check a value, but one matching input alone does not prove equivalence.

items.tutor_behavior: Multiply both x and 4 by 3.
Combine the x² terms separately from the x terms.
Distribute 4 to both terms.

solution_steps.explanation: Distribute 2 and then distribute the subtraction sign.
Combine each group and write in standard form.

items.tutor_behavior: Treat subtraction before the second parentheses as multiplication by -1.

items.prompt: Rewrite 6x²+9x by extracting the greatest common factor.
items.tutor_behavior: Extract the complete numerical and variable common factor.

solution_steps.explanation: Distribute each term of x+4 across x+1.

items.tutor_behavior: Account for all four partial products.
The negative factor changes the sign of every product.
Expand 4x(x+2), then combine the x² terms.

items.prompt: Rewrite 10x²-15x using its greatest common factor.
items.tutor_behavior: Both terms share 5x; keep the subtraction sign inside.
Distribute first, then combine 10x and 4x.
Only the x² terms combine; 7x and 5 are unlike.

items.prompt: Rewrite 12x²+8x using its greatest common factor.
items.tutor_behavior: Extract 4x and verify by distribution.
Form all four signed products before combining like terms.
Distribute both factors and combine x² and x terms separately.
Distribute -2 to all three terms before combining x² terms.

items.prompt: Rewrite 15x²+20x using its greatest common factor.
items.tutor_behavior: The greatest common factor is 5x.

items.prompt: A student says (x+2)² and x²+4 are equivalent. Is the student correct?
items.explanation_prompt: Explain the missing term and give the correct equivalent standard form.
items.explanation_guidance: The square means (x+2)(x+2). The two cross products total 4x, so the equivalent standard form is x²+4x+4.
items.tutor_behavior: Require the two cross products and the complete trinomial.

items.prompt: A rectangle has length 3x+2 and width x-1. Rewrite its perimeter in simplest form.
items.tutor_behavior: Use P=2(length)+2(width), then distribute and combine.
Multiply both terms by 7.
A leading negative is a factor of -1 applied to every term.
Combine terms by matching powers.

items.prompt: Rewrite 18x²-12x using its greatest common factor.
items.tutor_behavior: Extract 6x from both terms.
Multiplication distributes over addition.
Expand 2x(x+3) and combine the x² terms.

items.prompt: At x=2, two expressions have the same value. Does that single check prove they are equivalent?
accepted_answers: no one value is not enough
items.tutor_behavior: Equivalence requires equality for every allowed input; use algebraic rewriting to prove it.

items.prompt: A square has side x+3. Rewrite its area in standard polynomial form.
items.tutor_behavior: Area=(x+3)(x+3); include both cross products.
Distribute both signed factors, then combine like powers.
Expand the product to 2x²+7x-4, then subtract 3x.

items.prompt: Rewrite 9x²-3x by extracting a common factor, then name the property used.
items.tutor_behavior: Reverse the distributive property by extracting 3x.

items.prompt: Two adjacent rectangles have areas 2x²+6x and x²-2x. Rewrite their total area in simplest form.
items.tutor_behavior: Add the area expressions and combine like terms.

distribution.teacher_signal: Does not multiply every term or misses a partial product

negative_distribution.teacher_signal: Changes only one sign when distributing a negative

combine_like_terms.teacher_signal: Combines unlike powers or leaves like terms separate

multi_step_rewrite.teacher_signal: Uses operations in an order that changes the expression

gcf_rewrite.teacher_signal: Extracts an incomplete or incorrect common factor

equivalence_test.teacher_signal: Judges equivalence by appearance or one input only

property_reasoning.teacher_signal: Cannot connect a rewrite to the distributive property

geometric_expression.teacher_signal: Builds or simplifies a geometric polynomial expression incorrectly
